title: Colour Lab: synchronized picker, HEX, RGB, HSL, alpha, copy
learningObjectives: Explain colour lab: synchronized picker, hex, rgb, hsl, alpha, copy and implement a maintainable CSS workflow or lab.

understand.concept: A Colour Lab combines a native colour picker with editable HEX, RGB, HSL, and alpha controls, a live swatch, and copyable CSS snippets. A robust implementation keeps one canonical colour state and derives all displayed formats from it.
understand.whyItMatters: The lab must validate input, keep controls synchronized, preserve the last valid colour after invalid edits, and provide accessible labels and copy feedback. Native input type=color does not provide every alpha workflow.
understand.analogy: The lab is a control panel with several readouts for one selected colour; changing one control should update the other readouts consistently.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the design; implementation must follow browser APIs, CSS behaviour, and accessibility requirements.

explain.narrative: The starter synchronizes a native picker and six-digit HEX value with a live swatch. RGB/HSL/alpha conversion, validation messaging, and clipboard support are required extensions.

practise.guidedTask: Extend the lab to synchronize RGB and HSL fields, support alpha, show validation errors without losing the last valid colour, and copy a CSS snippet with permission-aware feedback.
practise.independentTask: Build a small production-minded example. Validate input, keep the baseline usable, and document browser and accessibility checks.
hints: Keep one canonical state for synchronized controls.
Use textContent for user-generated output rather than unsafe HTML insertion.
Test keyboard operation and invalid input.

questions.prompt: Why should the lab derive multiple colour formats from one canonical state?
questions.explanation: One source of truth prevents the picker, text fields, and preview from drifting apart.

questions.prompt: What is essential for an interactive CSS lab?
options: Accessible controls, validation, and synchronized preview
questions.answer: Accessible controls, validation, and synchronized preview
questions.explanation: A useful lab must be operable, robust to invalid input, and consistent across its controls.
